United States Department of the Interior
BUREAU OF OUTDOOR RECREATION WASHINGTON, D.C. 20240
MAY 5 1972
Memorandum
To:
Chief, Office of Environmental Quality
Bureau of Sport Fisheries and Wildlife
From:
Deputy Director, Bureau of Outdoor Recreation
Subject:
Review of Draft Environmental Statement for H.R. 13111 -
Endangered Species Legislation
Pursuant to your request of March 29, 1972, on the subject draft environmental statement we offer the following comments for your consideration.
0
Environmental Impact of the Proposed Action (page 11). It is stated that the primary effect of this legislative action is not to change the environment but to prevent change and restore the natural order. Also, to conserve and protect some endangered species it will be necessary to set aside certain areas and maintain them for the use of the species in question. Generally, the areas to be set aside will not be available for commercial use such as agriculture. "This will adversely affect those groups interested in developing the area; however, these preserves will expand the public domain and may provide additional areas for recreational use."
We are of the opinion that the statement needs to address itself to elaborating and clarifying the above paragraph, particularly as it pertains to agricultural and possible recreational use. Agriculture is not a "clean" commercial use of the land, because there are many spin-off beneficial uses of agricultural lands. Also, it is recommended that other "restricted commercial uses" in addition to agriculture be presented and discussed. Since "these preserves will expand the public domain and may provide additional areas for recreational use" it is recommended that several examples of the permitted recreational use be presented and discussed.
Irreversible and Irretrievable Commitments of Resources Which Would be Involved in the Proposed Action Should it be Implemented (page 19). It is stated that, "The purpose of the proposed legislation is to protect, conserve, and propagate a renewable resource. The methods employed to reach this goal will not require the irreversible or irretrievable commitment of natural resources."
